A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Molmo/PixMo research. The complete text, tables, and figures support reliable matching. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes substantial appendices A–H, all inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original Molmo results on 11 benchmarks, a human preference study, and AndroidControl in Section 4, Table 1, and Figures 2 and 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds model/data ablations, clock-reading, pointing, and text-only experiments in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The specified connector order changes from MLP projection followed by pooling in v1 Section 2 to pooling followed by MLP projection in v2 Section 2. v2 also introduces an optional high-resolution post-training adaptation in Appendix D. The core model family and two-stage pipeline remain; expanded architectural descriptions do not establish wholesale changes to the released models.

E1.justification: v2 adds text-only knowledge, reasoning, mathematics, and programming evaluations, plus experiments incorporating Tulu 3 training data. It also evaluates real-world clocks from COCO, OpenImages, and Clock Movies, and introduces dedicated captioning and pointing evaluation sets. The original Flickr Count benchmark is retained as PixMo-Count, rather than being a new benchmark.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Llama-3.2V-11B-Instruct and Llama-3.2V-90B-Instruct. The Chameleon-7B/30B human-evaluation entries in v1 Figure 4 are omitted from v2's reported comparison. Additional comparisons introduce a specialized clock-reading model, the underlying Qwen2-7B language model, and a broader externally reported Chatbot Arena comparator set in Tables 9, 10, and 13.

E3.justification: New studies introduce caption scoring, point-assignment evaluation, controlled crop configurations, high-resolution post-training, and a balanced 500-question human ablation study distinct from the retained main study. Reported PixMo-Points image counts also change from 428k to 223k, and point-explanation images from 29k to 14k. These count revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun; newly disclosed original settings belong under D1.

E4.justification: v1 lacks corresponding systematic ablations. v2 Tables 2–5 and 15 test encoders, crops, dropout, pooling, caption conditioning, data scale/composition, and counting representations. Appendix D additionally investigates crop-mismatch failures and recovery, text-only knowledge loss and mitigation, opaque AI2D boxes, human-evaluation ties, and the relationship between caption quality and downstream accuracy.

E5.justification: v2 adds explicit 95% confidence intervals for externally reported Arena scores in Table 9 and a Pearson correlation/least-squares analysis across 22 ablations in Figure 9. Conversely, the boxes and whiskers accompanying v1's own-study Elo scores in Figure 4 disappear when those results are tabulated. Neither version documents repeated training seeds.

E6.justification: All 25 retained Table 1 rows have unchanged academic scores, including Molmo-72B's 81.2 average. However, v2 adds extensive ablation and supplementary results, including Molmo-7B-D's 68.2% clock-reading accuracy, Molmo-72B's 75.2 pointing F1, and text-only performance losses and recovery experiments. The new Arena scores concern a different evaluation, not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix C newly defines caption precision and recall through atomic-statement matching and consistency judgments, then defines cap F1 from their image-averaged values. Appendix D specifies assignment-based pointing precision/recall and no-target cases. These are new task-specific mathematical definitions, beyond merely restating the standard F1 formula; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about open Molmo/PixMo models, avoiding proprietary-VLM distillation for the main models, and competitive benchmark/human performance persist. v2's introduction additionally presents overlapping cropping, efficient multi-annotation training, and systematic model/data design insights as contributions. The more explicit abstract comparisons largely repeat claims already present in v1's introduction.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations and qualifications concerning crop-mismatch failures, weaker reasoning performance, text-only knowledge loss, caption-metric errors, and differences between its human evaluation and Chatbot Arena. It explicitly cautions that caption/downstream correlation does not establish causality. Appendix H also acknowledges that using closed text-only LLMs leaves the data-generation pipeline incompletely open.

D1.justification: v1 gives a high-level recipe and promises full data and training-code releases; v2 states that datasets and source code are available. Appendices A–C and Tables 6–8 add architecture dimensions, optimizer settings, sampling rates, prompts, preprocessing, precision and gradient handling, sequence limits, evaluation details, H100 hardware, and training times. Much of this is newly disclosed information about retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds an extensive related-work discussion in Appendix H, covering contrastive encoders, multimodal architectures, instruction data, synthetic documents, grounding, and dependence on closed LLMs. It substantively compares PixMo with approaches such as GRES/RefCOCO and ExpertQA and discusses alternative architectures. This substantially expands v1's brief introductory positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction and technical exposition are extensively rewritten and subdivided. Data and Training become separate sections, the Release Plan section disappears, and appendices organize model, training, evaluation, results, ablations, data, examples, and related work. Existing material, including annotator questions, is relocated. The title also changes 'Multimodal Models' to 'Vision-Language Models.'

P2.justification: v2 redraws the architecture figure and adds dataset-overview, cropping, tokenization, mixture, diagnostic, and example figures, alongside numerous experimental and implementation tables. Table 1 gains Elo score/rank columns while v1's benchmark-summary and Elo plots disappear. The openness comparison is retained and relocated from v1 Figure 3 to v2 Figure 11.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's lack of controlled ablation evidence and reproducibility detail through Section 6 and Appendices A–E. It also exposes important failures and applicability limits, including crop sensitivity, text-only degradation, and less favorable independent human rankings. These gains outweigh the lost own-study Elo uncertainty display and occasional overclaims, such as the RealWorldQA summary not matching Table 1. The improvement comes from stronger evidence and transparency, while retained benchmark scores remain unchanged.
